briefing.text: The hypothesis has two parts: KIT mutation enrichment and focal amplification enrichment in Triple-WT. List every file and column and check for any copy-number, GISTIC, segment or amplification variable. ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY measures whole-genome ploidy, not focal amplification, so do not use it as a proxy. If no focal-amplification variable exists, decide explicitly how a result on the KIT half alone bears on the label, and say in the reasoning which part could not be assessed.
briefing.reason: The claim is compound and the data may cover only part of it. How the team handles the missing half decides the label, and a ploidy proxy would be invalid.

briefing.text: Use the study's own subtype assignment, MUTATION_TYPE in data_clinical_sample.txt (BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants, RAS_Hotspot_Mutants, NF1_Any_Mutants, Triple_WT, plus NA), as the grouping. Exclude NA samples rather than treating them as wild-type. Re-deriving subtypes from the MAF can disagree with this assignment, which is hierarchical (BRAF > RAS > NF1).
briefing.reason: Wrong grouping, or counting NA as Triple-WT, changes the comparison groups directly.

briefing.text: The MAF includes silent, intronic, UTR, flank and RNA variants. Before calling a sample KIT-mutant, keep only protein-altering classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame, Splice_Site). Melanoma TMB is very high and differs by subtype (NF1 is highest, Triple-WT tends to be low), so passenger KIT missense mutations in high-TMB subtypes can distort the comparison. Classify KIT mutations as known oncogenic/hotspot (exons 11/13/17, e.g. W557, V559, V560, L576P, K642E, D816, N822) or other. Report the analysis both ways (hotspot/oncogenic KIT and any protein-altering KIT), compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS across subtypes, and optionally adjust for log TMB.
briefing.reason: How a KIT mutation is defined can change the direction of the enrichment result, given the large TMB differences between subtypes.

briefing.text: Count at the sample level: collapse to one KIT status per Tumor_Sample_Barcode and match barcodes to SAMPLE_ID. Use as denominators only samples that were actually sequenced (present in the MAF or gene panel matrix). Check for patients with more than one sample and deduplicate. Report n per group.
briefing.reason: Counting mutation rows, or using unsequenced samples as denominators, distorts the frequencies.

briefing.text: Triple_WT is small (about 46 samples) and KIT mutation is rare, so expected counts in a 2x2 table will be small. Use Fisher's exact test with an odds ratio and CI plus per-group percentages, not a chi-square test or percentages alone. Also compare Triple-WT against each other subtype separately.
briefing.reason: With these small counts, the choice of test determines whether any difference is judged meaningful.

briefing.text: data_mutsig.txt gives cohort-wide gene significance (rank, q) and has no subtype information. It cannot show enrichment in a subtype. Use it only to say whether KIT is significantly mutated overall, and do the enrichment test from the MAF plus clinical data.
briefing.reason: This stops a category error that could wrongly be read as evidence for the hypothesis.

briefing.text: KIT-mutant melanomas cluster in acral, mucosal and chronically sun-damaged sites, which are also often BRAF/NRAS wild-type. Cross-tabulate KIT status with SITE_OF_PRIMARY_TUMOR and UV_SIGNATURE and report this as context. The hypothesis is descriptive (whether the subtype is characterized by the feature), so confounding by site explains an association; it is not by itself a reason to change the label.
briefing.reason: This keeps the team from changing its label on causal grounds when the claim is descriptive.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed that a compound claim ('KIT mutations AND focal amplifications') can be labelled True when only one conjunct is tested; neither tested whether the untestable half should instead move the label to Not verifiable.
Both assumed the study's MUTATION_TYPE grouping is the definition of Triple-WT and that the 43 NA-subtype samples are missing at random (Team B notes 4 KIT-mutant samples are among them).
Both treated 'enrichment' as Triple-WT vs pooled other subtypes; Team A found no significant difference vs NF1, so the result may depend on the comparator choice.

Both treat samples as independent units, without stating whether Primary and Metastasis samples are mixed or whether multiple samples per patient exist (Team A found 2 duplicate patients; Team B reports 0 duplicate sample IDs but did not check patient duplicates).
unused_evidence: data_gene_panel_matrix.txt: 13 of 359 samples have NA in the sequencing column, so they were not sequenced. Team A used 346 sequenced barcodes; Team B reports a '100% ID match' and may have counted unsequenced samples as KIT wild-type in the denominators.

MAF columns TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks / Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks: these are gene-level pan-cancer peak annotations, not per-sample copy-number calls. Team B noted them; neither said whether they can stand in for per-sample focal amplification. They probably cannot, but the decision should be stated.
ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY: Team A ruled it out as a proxy; Team B noted it but did not say why it was rejected.
SAMPLE_TYPE / REGIONAL_VS_PRIMARY (Primary vs Metastasis): neither team stratified by sample type, which could confound subtype–KIT associations.
unresolved_weak_points: Both named the untestable focal-amplification half as their weakest point and both only reported it. Neither resolved whether a compound hypothesis with one conjunct untestable can be labelled True.
Team A: KIT counts are small (6 events) and the NF1 comparison is not significant. It reported this but did not resolve it.
Team B: excluded the 4 KIT-mutant NA-subtype samples and called the result 'robust' without showing a sensitivity analysis. It also ran no TMB adjustment and no hotspot vs any-variant distinction.
second_readings: 'Characterized by enrichment of KIT mutations and focal amplifications' can be read as KIT mutations plus KIT focal amplifications (a KIT-locus claim), or as KIT mutations plus focal amplifications generally (genome-wide CNA burden). Either way, per-sample copy-number data are needed.
'Enrichment' can mean higher than the other subtypes pooled, or higher than every other subtype. These give different answers if the NF1 group is not different.
Under one reading, the label rests on whether the whole claim is supported; under the other, on whether any testable part is supported. That choice decides between True and Not verifiable.
challenge.verdict: The KIT-enrichment finding looks sound but rests on few events and depends on the comparator. Both teams assumed without testing that a compound hypothesis can be labelled True when its focal-amplification half has no data, and that is the main threat to the agreed label. Trust is moderate to low until the teams justify that choice.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Confirm with an exhaustive search that no file has a per-sample copy-number or focal-amplification call (the MAF amplification-peak columns are gene-level annotations). If so, does your rule for compound claims justify 'True' when one conjunct cannot be assessed, or does it change the label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Rerun the Fisher test for Triple_WT vs each other subtype separately and vs pooled, and restrict to one sample per patient and to metastasis-only samples. Does the enrichment hold against all comparators, and does the result change the method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: As a sensitivity check, assign the NA-subtype sequenced samples (including any KIT-mutant ones) to Triple_WT and then to the rest. Does the KIT result with 6 events survive both assignments?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: data_gene_panel_matrix.txt lists 13 samples with NA sequencing status. Recount your Fisher table using only sequenced samples as denominators. Does the result or the method change?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You found only gene-level amplification-peak annotations and ploidy. Given no per-sample focal-amplification variable, test whether your labelling rule for a two-part claim supports 'True', and say explicitly why the untested half does not lead to 'Not verifiable'.

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Repeat the KIT comparison separately against each other subtype (BRAF, RAS, NF1), with hotspot-only KIT and with TMB adjustment. Does enrichment persist vs the high-TMB NF1 group, and does that change your method?
QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Check for patients with more than one sample and for Primary vs Metastasis mixing, and rerun with one sample per patient. Does the result hold?

findings.question: In hypothesis-evaluation benchmarks for cancer genomics, how should a compound claim (A and B) be labelled when the data support A but contain no variables to assess B? Supported, or not verifiable?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web: I found no explicit cancer-genomics benchmark rule. The closest convention is FEVER-style claim verification (Supported / Refuted / NotEnoughInfo). There, Supported needs evidence for the whole claim, and evidence often has to be composed from several pieces. Under that logic, 'A supported, B unassessable' maps to Not verifiable, not Supported. The asymmetry is that a clearly contradicted A makes the conjunction False whatever B is. The task's own definition ('no relevant variables to support or reject') is ambiguous for partly testable claims, so the team should state its reasoning explicitly.

findings.question: In TCGA/Firehose Oncotator-annotated MAFs, do columns such as TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks describe per-sample copy-number status or gene-level pan-cancer GISTIC peak annotations?
findings.answer: Most likely gene-level pan-cancer GISTIC peak annotations, not per-sample copy-number status. The pages I read do not define the column directly. Oncotator annotates each variant with 'variant- and gene-centric information' from pooled external public resources, and its MAF headers list TCGAScape with a fixed datasource version (110405, per a search snippet). Together with domain knowledge, these columns say whether the mutated gene falls in a significant amplification or deletion peak across many tumours in the Broad TCGA/Tumorscape copy-number portals. So they give no evidence about focal amplification in a given sample. Suggested check: the value should be the same for every row of the same Hugo_Symbol.
